svg.aria-label: Every change hits the same fences. They never argue, and they grow. On the left, the agents. Every agent in every workflow looks up every definition and caller with code search before a change, is nudged by the agent hooks on every edit, has every workflow step checked by the step gates, and has its code formatted by the pre-commit hook on every commit. /bkit-plan decides the tests each feature adds to the fences (unit, integration or end-to-end). /bkit-build writes each test first, sees it fail, then hits every fence; the pre-push hook sends problems back before they leave your laptop. When a CI lane goes red, its logs give /bkit-debug the context to fix it. When CI is green, the change passes through and /bkit-ship merges it, re-checked on the merge commit. On the right, the fences, nearest and lightest first: code search on every lookup, agent hooks on every edit, step gates on every step, the pre-commit hook on every commit, the pre-push hook on every push, and CI, the strongest, on every push and pull request. The step gates are scripts, not prompts: a step missing its verdict or files can't finish, whatever the agent says. The pre-commit hook formats only the files being committed, so it takes seconds, and your own quick checks can go there too. CI runs integration, end-to-end and live-site tests, and one check fails if any lane failed, was skipped or ran no tests. Hooks, agents and CI run the same commands, and in cloud mode CI's answer starts debug or ship by itself.
